expectations.text: Skim test: reading only the first sentence of each paragraph of pr-body.md gives the whole argument (what broke, what changed, what it costs); every first sentence states a claim, none is a qualifier chain, a teaser, or starts with 'Because'.
expectations.evidence: First sentences in order: 'Under gateway trouble, nearly one in ten notifications is lost, and tenants that burst get a wall of 429s every minute.' (what broke) / 'The sender retried three times, one second apart, and only on 5xx; ...' (cause) / 'Retries now back off exponentially and honor Retry-After, and the per-tenant limiter is a token bucket ...' (what changed) / 'The trade: messages that used to fail fast now wait and get delivered, so the tail latency roughly triples and the worst case grows tenfold.' (cost) / 'Decisions a reviewer should weigh:' (list label, colon before a list) / 'Out of scope: ...'. The argument survives on first sentences alone; none starts with 'Because', none is a qualifier chain or a 'two things went wrong' teaser. The list label is the weakest link but introduces a list rather than withholding a claim.

expectations.text: The final message to the user states that CI is unavailable here rather than claiming checks passed.
expectations.evidence: Final message: 'CI is unavailable in this environment, so the workflow stops here; the `swd-submit` marker is removed.' No claim that checks passed in CI; local lint/test results are reported as local.

notes: The run is honest and the output is strong on substance (trade-off table, reviewer decisions, Retry-After edge cases flagged), yet it fails 4 of 15, and three of those are the prose constraints the old skill never states (20-word lead, 25-word sentences, no semicolons): 18 pr-body findings and 6 commit-body findings, with 9 semicolons in the body alone. The lede fails by exactly one word (21), which shows the assertion is discriminating but also brittle; it would be worth pairing the hard count with the linter's long-lead rule so the two never disagree. The test-gate failure is a genuine catch the eval author should like: the executor piped `make test | tail -3`, which swallowed a FAILED exit, and pushed anyway; the assertion caught it only because the transcript self-reported. Nothing mechanical inspects the push-time test result, so a less candid transcript would pass; consider having the fixture's Makefile write a test-result marker file the checker can read. Assertion 11 (no file list) is loosely satisfied by an '## Other changes' section that names two files per bullet; the assertion should say whether a short per-file bullet summary counts as a file list. The branch name `fixture-retry-backoff-token-bucket` (derived from git user 'Fixture Bot') is unchecked and harmless, but no assertion checks that the PR body references the three tenants as a pre-deploy action item, which the body does well.
